info.title: SKDY RAG Server API
info.description:
HTTP API for the SKDY RAG Server. Mounted under `/api/v1`.

**Contract**: the OpenAPI schema is the single source of truth for the Web UI; client types are generated from it.

**Error envelope**: every 4xx/5xx returns `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "request_id": "...", "details": {}}}`.

post.description:
Upload one or more documents to a collection and start ingestion.

Two mutually-exclusive modes on the same endpoint:

- **Single** (legacy, M2): send ``file``. Returns ``202`` with a
  ``DocumentUploadResponse``; behavior is unchanged from M2 except the
  addition of a file-extension check (415) beside the MIME check
  (double validation per DEV_SPEC).
- **Batch** (M5): send ``files[]``. All files go to the same
  collection. Returns ``202`` with a ``BatchUploadResponse`` carrying
  a ``batch_id`` and one result per file (``accepted`` → ``task_id``
  to poll, ``skipped`` → duplicate, ``rejected`` → structured error).
  A single file's validation / ingestion failure never blocks the
  others.

Limits: per-file size ``WEB_API_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES`` (413), batch file
count ``WEB_API_UPLOAD_MAX_BATCH_FILES`` and batch total
``WEB_API_UPLOAD_MAX_BATCH_BYTES`` (413), extension + MIME allow-lists
(415). Unknown collection → 404. There is no SSE — clients poll
``GET /tasks/{id}`` for each accepted file.

schema.title: Response Upload Collection Document Api V1 Collections  Collection Id  Documents Post

delete.description: Coordinated delete across vector store + BM25 + image storage.

get.description:
Return the current status of an ingestion task.

The task registry is process-local. A task that cannot be found
returns ``404`` with envelope code ``TASK_NOT_FOUND``. Frontends
poll this endpoint after ``POST /collections/{id}/documents`` until
the status reaches ``succeeded`` or ``failed``.
Aggregate quality, latency and ingestion signals for the overview UI.

post.summary: Run a hybrid query against a collection
post.description:
Run retrieval and return citations + diagnostics.

M3: ``collection=name`` routes the query to the per-collection
``HybridSearch`` (EngineCache) — fixing the v0.2 limitation where
every collection silently queried the default index.

Submit a query and return immediately.

M3 batch 2: the query runs in a background thread; poll
``GET /queries/{query_id}/result`` for the outcome. ``task_id``
equals ``query_id`` (and the trace id).

get.description:
Poll an async query (M3 batch 2).

``pending`` / ``running`` → keep polling; ``succeeded`` populates
``result``; ``failed`` populates ``error``. Unknown ids return 404
``QUERY_NOT_FOUND``.

Return the per-stage trace for a previously run query.

Every query recorded by the Web API stores its trace under
``query_id == trace_id``, so this is a straight store lookup.

Return the per-stage trace for a previously run ingestion.

Ingestion traces are recorded with ``trace_id == task_id``. When the
trace is missing but the task still exists (e.g. recorded before this
feature, or trace persistence failed), return 200 with empty stages —
the ingestion *record* is real even if its timeline is gone.
Return image bytes for the given image ID.

AsyncQueryAccepted.title: AsyncQueryAccepted
AsyncQueryAccepted.description:
``POST /collections/{id}/queries/async`` response (M3 batch 2).

Returns immediately with the query id; poll ``GET /queries/{id}/result``
until it reaches ``succeeded`` / ``failed``. ``task_id`` equals
``query_id`` (and the trace id) so one id drives result + trace.

result.description: The query response, present only when ``status`` is ``succeeded``.

error.description: Structured error, present only when ``status`` is ``failed``.

AsyncQueryResult.title: AsyncQueryResult
AsyncQueryResult.description:
``GET /queries/{query_id}/result`` response (M3 batch 2).

Poll until ``status`` is ``succeeded`` (``result`` populated) or
``failed`` (``error`` populated). ``pending`` / ``running`` mean the
background query is still in flight.

document_id.title: Document Id
document_id.description: Stable document UUID (``uuid5`` of collection+source path). ``None`` for rejected files (never written to storage).

task_id.title: Task Id
task_id.description: Ingestion task to poll for ``accepted`` files; ``None`` for ``skipped``/``rejected``.

error.description: Structured error for ``rejected`` files. Same shape as the HTTP error envelope — branch on ``error.code`` (``UNSUPPORTED_FILE_TYPE`` / ``UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`` / ``FILE_TOO_LARGE`` / ``DUPLICATE_FILENAME``).

total.title: Total
total.description: Number of files in the batch.

BatchUploadResponse.title: BatchUploadResponse
BatchUploadResponse.description:
``POST /collections/{id}/documents`` batch response (M5).

One batch uploads many files to the same collection. Each file is
validated and submitted independently — a single rejection never
blocks the others, and accepted files each carry their own
``task_id`` for async polling. ``total == accepted + skipped + rejected``.

files.title: Files
files.description: Batch of documents; all go to this collection.

text.title: Text
text.description: Raw chunk text for snippet rendering.

Citation.title: Citation
Citation.description:
One retrievable chunk referenced by the answer.

The 1-based index matches the ``[1]`` markers in the answer text so
the Web UI can render clickable inline references.

example.text: 员工年假标准：入职满 1 年不满 10 年，每年 5 天；…

caption.title: Caption
caption.description: Image caption (if multimodal enrichment was enabled).

CitationImage.title: CitationImage
CitationImage.description:
Image associated with a citation.

``url`` is always a *relative* path (``/api/v1/images/{id}``) so the
frontend can resolve it against the configured API base URL.
Local filesystem paths MUST NOT leak into the API.

dense.title: Dense
dense.description: Cosine similarity from the dense retriever (0–1).

sparse.title: Sparse
sparse.description: BM25 score from the sparse retriever (raw, not normalised).

fusion.title: Fusion
fusion.description: Reciprocal Rank Fusion score — sum of ``1 / (k + rank_i)`` across the input rankings (default ``k = 60``). **Higher is better.** Range is roughly ``(0, len(rankings)]``; values for the top hit are typically small (e.g. ~0.016 for k=60). See ``src/core/query_engine/fusion.py::reciprocal_rank_fusion``.

rerank.title: Rerank
rerank.description: Score from the rerank stage (provider-specific range).

CitationScores.title: CitationScores
CitationScores.description:
Per-stage scores for a single citation.

Every field is nullable because a chunk may appear in only one
retrieval branch (e.g. dense-only query) or have no rerank applied.

name.title: Name
name.description: Human-readable collection name. Must be unique.

chunk_count.title: Chunk Count
chunk_count.description: Total chunks indexed across all documents.

CollectionDetail.title: CollectionDetail
CollectionDetail.description:
``GET /collections/{id}`` response — same as summary for now.

Kept as a separate type so future fields (e.g. configuration overrides)
can be added without breaking the list response.

CollectionListResponse.title: CollectionListResponse

chunk_count.title: Chunk Count
chunk_count.description: Total chunks indexed across all documents.

CollectionSummary.title: CollectionSummary
CollectionSummary.description: Lightweight collection row for the list endpoint.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: Optional short message for the diagnostic page.

chunk_count.title: Chunk Count
chunk_count.description: Number of chunks written to the vector store.

image_count.title: Image Count
image_count.description: Number of images extracted and indexed.

file_hash.title: File Hash
file_hash.description: SHA-256 of the raw file. Used to detect duplicate uploads.

last_task_id.title: Last Task Id
last_task_id.description: Most recent ingestion task ID, if any.

last_query_id.title: Last Query Id
last_query_id.description: Most recent query that cited this document, if any (M3 batch 2). Lets the UI jump from a document back to the query's trace.

last_error.description: Structured error from the last failed task (if any). Same shape as the top-level HTTP error envelope — branch on ``last_error.code``.

DocumentDetail.title: DocumentDetail
DocumentDetail.description:
``GET /documents/{id}`` response — extends summary with ingestion refs.

``last_task_id`` lets the frontend jump straight to the task detail
page when ``status`` is anything other than ``ready``.

chunk_count.title: Chunk Count
chunk_count.description: Number of chunks written to the vector store.

image_count.title: Image Count
image_count.description: Number of images extracted and indexed.

DocumentSummary.title: DocumentSummary
DocumentSummary.description: Lightweight row for collection document list.

task_id.title: Task Id
task_id.description: Ingestion task ID; poll ``GET /tasks/{id}`` for status.

DocumentUploadResponse.title: DocumentUploadResponse
DocumentUploadResponse.description:
``POST /collections/{id}/documents`` response.

The synchronous-first design returns the created document + the
ingestion task ID immediately. The frontend then polls ``/tasks/{id}``
for status (no SSE in M1 — see TODO M3 #18).

MCPKeySecretResponse.title: MCPKeySecretResponse
MCPKeySecretResponse.description: Returned only by create/rotate; ``api_key`` is never listable.

OverviewMetric.title: OverviewMetric
OverviewMetric.description: Current and previous-period value for one decision metric.

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. ``null`` means no more pages.

has_more.title: Has More
has_more.description: Convenience flag; equivalent to ``next_cursor is not None``.

PageInfo.title: PageInfo
PageInfo.description:
Cursor pagination metadata.

The cursor is opaque to clients; they should pass back whatever
``next_cursor`` they got in the previous response.

``next_cursor`` is required + nullable: every response carries the
field, with ``null`` meaning "no more pages". This avoids the
front-end having to distinguish between "field missing" and
"field is null".

configured.title: Configured
configured.description: Whether the Provider has the required configuration (without exposing the value).

ready.title: Ready
ready.description: Whether the Provider is currently reachable / usable.

model.title: Model
model.description: Configured model name, if any. Omitted if not configured.

ProviderStatus.title: ProviderStatus
ProviderStatus.description:
Per-Provider presence + readiness.

The ``configured`` and ``ready`` booleans are the only signals the
frontend should depend on. Detailed model names are exposed because
the Web overview page needs them, but secrets are NEVER returned.

trace_id.title: Trace Id
trace_id.description: Trace ID for this query; pass to ``GET /queries/{query_id}/trace`` for the full per-stage breakdown.

dense_count.title: Dense Count
dense_count.description: Chunks returned by the dense retriever.

sparse_count.title: Sparse Count
sparse_count.description: Chunks returned by the sparse retriever.

degraded.title: Degraded
degraded.description: True if at least one stage fell back due to a failure.

degraded_reasons.title: Degraded Reasons
degraded_reasons.description: Human-readable reasons; frontend should display but never branch business logic on these strings. Use ``degraded`` for the boolean.

QueryDiagnostics.title: QueryDiagnostics
QueryDiagnostics.description:
Per-stage counts, latency, and degradation signals.

Listed in the v0.1 contract — frontend may render these on the
Playground / Trace page. All counts are nullable so the backend
can skip reporting a stage it didn't run (e.g. rerank when
``enable_rerank=false``).

top_k.title: Top K
top_k.description: Maximum number of chunks to return. Hard-capped to 50.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: Retrieval mode: hybrid (default), dense-only, or sparse-only.

enable_rerank.title: Enable Rerank
enable_rerank.description: If false, the rerank stage is skipped. Equivalent to disabling the rerank provider in settings but for a single request.

answer.title: Answer
answer.description: Final answer text. In v0.1 this is ``null`` — we return chunks and citations, not generated answers. See PRODUCTION §10.

QueryResponse.title: QueryResponse
QueryResponse.description:
``POST /collections/{id}/queries`` response.

``query_id`` is the query record ID; pass it to
``GET /queries/{id}/trace`` for the full Trace JSON.
``answer`` is null in v0.1 — final answer generation is out of scope
(see PRODUCTION §10 "final answer generation as optional independent stage").

citations.text: 员工年假标准：入职满 1 年不满 10 年，每年 5 天；…

rerank_success_rate.title: Rerank Success Rate
rerank_success_rate.description: Unavailable while reranking is not enabled/instrumented.

SystemHealth.title: SystemHealth
SystemHealth.description:
``GET /system/health`` response.

Top-level ``status`` is the worst of any dependency — frontend should
show a banner when this is anything other than ``ok``.

providers.title: Providers
providers.description: Map of component name (llm / embedding / vision) to its status. NEVER contains credentials.

features.title: Features
features.description: Optional capability flags (e.g. multimodal, image_captioning). Web UI may use these to hide unsupported actions.

SystemInfo.title: SystemInfo
SystemInfo.description:
``GET /system/info`` response.

Exposes the pluggable component layout + a per-Provider status map.

code.title: Code
code.description: Stable machine-readable code. Frontend branches on this, NEVER on ``message``. Same vocabulary as the top-level HTTP error envelope (``ErrorDetail.code``).

details.title: Details
details.description: Optional structured context (e.g. provider name, status code).

TaskError.title: TaskError
TaskError.description:
Structured error for async business operations.

Lives inside :class:`TaskStatusResponse` and
:class:`DocumentDetail` (as ``last_error``). Same shape and
branching rules as the top-level HTTP :class:`ErrorDetail`, but
scoped to "this thing I asked you to do, eventually failed" rather
than "this request couldn't even be processed".

current.title: Current
current.description: Items processed in this stage; ``null`` when unknown.

total.title: Total
total.description: Items expected in this stage; ``null`` when unknown.

percent.title: Percent
percent.description: Computed by the backend (0–100). Frontend must NOT recompute; different stages use different denominators.

message.title: Message
message.description: Short human-readable hint. Frontend may display but must NOT branch business logic on it.

TaskProgress.title: TaskProgress
TaskProgress.description:
Structured progress for the current pipeline stage.

``percent`` is the canonical value the frontend should display
(0–100). ``current``/``total`` stay for diagnostic views and are
nullable when the backend can't predict totals (e.g. some LLM
transforms).

progress.description: Current stage + progress. ``None`` when status is ``pending`` or any terminal state.

attempt.title: Attempt
attempt.description: Retry attempt count (0 for first try).

error.description: Structured error when the task finished in a failed state. Same shape as the top-level HTTP error envelope — frontend branches on ``error.code``, never on ``error.message``. ``None`` for any non-failed status.

id.title: Id
id.description: Trace ID (== query or ingestion ID).

TraceStage.title: TraceStage
TraceStage.description:
One stage inside a trace.

``method`` / ``provider`` are the dynamic-component hints the
Dashboard already uses to render provider-specific detail
(see DEV_SPEC §3.4.4 / §3.4.5).

embedding_token_usage.title: Embedding Token Usage
embedding_token_usage.description: Embedding input tokens consumed by query and document indexing operations.

query_embedding_tokens.title: Query Embedding Tokens
query_embedding_tokens.description: Embedding input tokens consumed by query-text vectorization.

ingestion_embedding_tokens.title: Ingestion Embedding Tokens
ingestion_embedding_tokens.description: Embedding input tokens consumed by document chunk vectorization.

embedding_token_usage_since.title: Embedding Token Usage Since
embedding_token_usage_since.description: UTC start of the earliest recorded usage event — lets the UI flag partial-period data.

TrafficMetrics.title: TrafficMetrics
TrafficMetrics.description:
Traffic + embedding token accounting (PRD docs/prd-embedding-token-metrics.md).

The three token fields are a unit: either all are numbers (accounting
is live for the window) or all are ``null`` (provider can't report
usage, or stats not wired). ``0`` is an honest "measured, nothing
consumed" answer — never converted to ``null``.
